entertainment.desc: बिग बॉस 20 के वीकेंड वार में सलमान खान ने गेमर स्काउट ओपी को जमकर क्लास लगाई. सलमान ने स्काउट की लॉयल्टी पर सवाल उठाए और कहा कि शो में बहन शब्द को पनौती हैं.

entertainment.title: 'आप बच्चा पैदा नहीं कर सकतीं', 41 की उम्र में एक्ट्रेस को हुई 'फर्टिलिटी' की चिंता, डॉक्टर की बात से हुईं परेशान
entertainment.desc: 'मिर्जापुर' फेम एक्ट्रेस श्वेता त्रिपाठी ने अपनी शादीशुदा जिंदगी की चुनौतियों पर बात की. एक्ट्रेस ने बताया कि जब उन्हें डॉक्टर ने उनकी कम फर्टिलिटी लेवल के बारे में बताया, तो उन्हें गहरा दुख पहुंचा था, क्योंकि वे नहीं चाहती थी कोई उन्हें बताए कि आप बच्चा पैदा नहीं कर सकतीं.

entertainment.title: दूरदर्शन का पौराणिक शो, जिसने उड़ाई बिजली विभाग की रातों की नींद, बत्ती गुल होने पर ट्रांसफॉर्मर जला देते थे लोग
entertainment.desc: पुराने 90 के दशक में दूरदर्शन पर कई शोज ऐसे आए, जिनका क्रेज अलग ही लेवल पर था। इनमें से ही एक था 'महाभारत'। इसे लेकर नीतीश भारद्वाज ने कई खुलासे किए। उन्होंने बताया कि बिजली विभाग की नाक में लोगों ने दम कर दिया था।

entertainment.title: Diljit Dosanjh Delhi Concert live: 'कोई रोककर दिखाए, मैं हूं पंजाब', दिलजीत दोसांझ ने दिल्ली कॉन्सर्ट में ललकारा, 'सतलुज' विवाद पर भी बोले
entertainment.desc: Diljit Dosanjh Delhi Concert: दिलजीत दोसांझ का दिल्ली कॉन्सर्ट 30 अक्तूबर को जेएलएन स्टेडियम में ऑर्गेनाइज किया गया, जिसमें 70 हजार की भीड़ पहुंची.

entertainment.title: 2 महीने में टूटी सगाई, मंगेतर ने किया चीट! दर्द में बिग बॉस एक्ट्रेस, रिश्ते पर तोड़ी चुप्पी
entertainment.desc: जिया शंकर ने इसी साल अगस्त में बॉयफ्रेंड करण धनक संग सगाई की न्यूज शेयर की है. एक्ट्रेस ने अपने ड्रीमी प्रपोजल की तस्वीरें फैंस संग साधा की थीं.

entertainment.title: Motivational Quotes By Piyush Mishra: 'मुझे भी मेरा शहर पसंद था, पर ये मालूम था कि आगे बढ़ना है तो मोह छोड़ना पड़ेगा'
entertainment.desc: Piyush Mishra Inspirational: 63 साल के हो रहे पीयूष मिश्रा एक मल्टी टैलेंटेड आर्टिस्ट है। सिंगिंग से लेकर एक्टिंग और गानों की लिरिक्स लिखने के अलावा भी मिश्रा कला जगह से जुड़े कई काम जानते हैं। उनका बचपन कठिनाईयों में बीता। लेकिन टैलेंट और मेहनत के दम पर आज पीयूष ने आज अपना एक मुकाम बना लिया है।

entertainment.title: Bigg Boss 20: कनिका मान ने बताई हिंसक बॉयफ्रेंड की कहानी, खून से भरने वाला था मांग, यंग की दोस्ती टूटी
entertainment.desc: 'बिग बॉस 20' का आज का एपिसोड थोड़ा इमोशनल हो गया। यंग को लग रहा है कि उनके सारे दोस्त धोखेबाज निकले। उनका कहना है कि घर से जाने के बाद वो किसी को याद नहीं रखेंगे। आम्रपाली और आसिफ की लड़ाई भी हुई। जानिए हाइलाइट्स।

entertainment.title: Kanika Sharma Saqib Saifi First Karwa Chauth: मुस्लिम धर्म में शादी करके ट्रोल हुई एक्ट्रेस, नहीं भूली रिवाज, मनाया करवाचौथ
entertainment.desc: मुस्लिम धर्म में शादी करने के बावजूद कनिका ने अपने रीति रिवाज नहीं छोड़े. उन्होंने धूमधाम से करवाचौथ मनाकर साबित कर दिया, उनके लिए फेस्टिवल एक इमोशन है, जिसे वो धर्म से जोड़कर नहीं देखतीं.

entertainment.title: पान मसाला एड विवाद: HC पहुंचे अजय देवगन, FDA नोटिस को किया चैलेंज
entertainment.desc: अजय देवगन ने पान मसाला ब्रांड से जुड़े FDA नोटिस के खिलाफ बॉम्बे हाईकोर्ट में याचिका दाखिल की है. उन्होंने FDA के नियमों की संवैधानिक वैधता पर सवाल उठाए हैं. एक्टर ने कहा कि कार्रवाई मैन्युफैक्चरिंग कंपनी के खिलाफ होनी चाहिए, न कि एंडोर्सर के खिलाफ.

entertainment.title: गुरप्रीत घुग्गी का लव गिल संग ₹5 करोड़ के समझौते और प्रेग्नेंसी के दावों पर फूटा गुस्सा, कहा- लड़की का तो सोचो
entertainment.desc: पंजाबी एक्टर गुरप्रीत घुग्गी ने हाल ही में लव गिल को लेकर बयान दिया है और उनका बचाव भी किया है। एक्टर ने प्रेग्नेंसी और 5 करोड़ रुपये के दावे पर कहा कि उनका नाम खराब करने की कोशिश की जा रही है और वो इसके लिए लीगल एक्शन लेंगे।

entertainment.title: Babil Khan House Tour: बाबिल का लैविश घर, पापा इरफान की फोटो-मूवी पोस्टर से सजा कोना, एंट्रेस पर लगी कुरान की आयतें
entertainment.desc: इरफान खान के बेटे और एक्टर बाबिल का मुंबई स्थित लोखंडवाला में खूबसूरत घर है. फराह खान ने उनके घर का टूर किया. ये घर इरफान की यादों से सजा है.

entertainment.title: एक ही कब्रिस्तान में दफन में मधुबाला-दिलीप कुमार, रिश्ते पर बहन का बड़ा खुलासा
entertainment.desc: मधुबाला और दिलीप कुमार का रिश्ता हिंदी सिनेमा की सबसे यादगार प्रेम कहानियों में से एक है. हाल ही में मुमताज ने दिलीप कुमार के मधुबाला से ब्रेकअप के पीछे उनकी दिल की बीमारी को कारण बताया था, जिसे मधुबाला की बहन मधुर भूषण ने खारिज किया.

entertainment.title: IAS तुकराम मुंढे की नोटिस को अजय देवगन ने बॉम्बे हाईकोर्ट में दी चुनौती, महाराष्ट्र FDA चीफ ने क्या कहा?
entertainment.desc: Tukaram Mundhe on Vimal Case: विमल इलायची के विज्ञापन के मामले में एफडीए चीफ तुकराम मुंढे ने शुक्रवार को बड़ा अपडेट साझा किया। उन्होंने बताया कि शाहरुख खान, टाइगर श्रॉफ और अजय देवगन को नोटिस जारी किए गए थे। इस मामले की प्रक्रिया के तहत सुनवाई पूरी हो चुकी है। सुनवाई खत्म होने के बाद अब इस एक्शन लिया जाना है। उन्होंने बताया कि अजय देवगन ने बॉम्बे हाईकोर्ट का रुख किया है।

entertainment.title: पलक तिवारी और इब्राहिन अली खान का 3 साल बाद रिश्ता खत्म! सैफ के बेटे ने लिया फैसला, साथ में शूटिंग कैंसल
entertainment.desc: पलक तिवारी और इब्राहिम अली खान का ब्रेकअप हो गया है। जी हां, उनके फैंस का ये सुनकर दिल टूट सकता है लेकिन रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, दोनों ने तीन साल से अधिक समय तक डेट करने के बाद राहें अलग कर ली हैं।

entertainment.title: मांग में सिंदूर-हाथ में छलनी, मुस्लिम एक्ट्रेस ने की करवाचौथ पूजा, यूजर्स बोले- धर्म बदल लिया?
entertainment.desc: शफक नाज ने इंस्टा पर करवाचौथ का अपना लुक शेयर किया. रेड साड़ी में वो स्टनिंग लगीं. उनके पति जीशान भी ट्रैडिशनल लुक में दिखे.

entertainment.title: 'बेटी भटक गई', नीम करोली बाबा की फिल्म में फंड देने के लिए प्रोड्यूसर ने छोड़ी थी एप्पल की नौकरी, घबराए पिता
entertainment.desc: 'हनुमान अंश' ने बॉक्स ऑफिस पर धमाल तो मचा ही दिया है। फिल्म भारत में ऐतिहासिक बनकर उभरी है। फिल्म की को-प्रोड्यूसर अनुप्रिया नागर ने हाल ही में बताया कि उनके पिता शुरू में खिलाफ थे कि वो नौकरी छोड़कर फिल्म बना रही हैं।

entertainment.title: Palak Tiwari-Ibrahim Ali Khan Break Up: 4 साल बाद टूटा इब्राहिम अली खान-पलक तिवारी का रिश्ता, दर्द में छोड़ा काम?
entertainment.desc: पलक तिवारी और इब्राहिम अली खान ने तीन साल की डेटिंग के बाद आपसी सहमति से ब्रेकअप कर लिया है. ब्रेकअप का फैसला इब्राहिम ने लिया है, हालांकि दोनों ने इसे सार्वजनिक रूप से कंफर्म नहीं किया है.

entertainment.title: लव गिल संग अफेयर, अबॉर्शन के लिए दिए 5 करोड़! गुरप्रीत गुग्गी बोले- मेरी इज्जत नहीं डूबेगी
entertainment.desc: लव गिल संग विवाद को लेकर पंजाबी एक्टर और कॉमेडियन गुरप्रीत सिंह गुग्गी का रिएक्शन वायरल हो रहा है. उन्होंने कहा कि चंद पैसों और व्यूज के लिए किसी की इमेज उछालना अच्छी बात नहीं है.

entertainment.title: 'मिर्जापुर' OTT रिलीज: सत्ता का भौकाली खेल घर बैठे देखिए, वो भी एक्सटेंडेड वर्जन, 2026 की टॉप-7 फिल्म
entertainment.desc: थिएटर में धूम मचाने के बाद मिर्जापुर की दुनिया ओटीटी पर लौट आई है। इसकी दमदार कास्ट के साथ फैंस के लिए एक और सरप्राइज है। ओटीटी पर फिल्म का एक्सटेंडेड वर्जन दिखाया जाएगा। जानिए फिल्म को किस प्लेटफॉर्म पर आज से ही देख सकते हैं।

entertainment.title: मधुबाला की कब्र पर घंटों रोते थे पिता, मकबरा बनाने के लिए इस्लाम के खिलाफ उठाया था कदम
entertainment.desc: मधुबाला की बहन मधुर भूषण ने एक्ट्रेस की कब्र से जुड़े कई भावुक किस्से सुनाए हैं. उन्होंने बताया कि पिता अताउल्लाह खान बेटी की कब्र पर इत्र डालते थे और सालों तक वहां बैठकर रोते थे. पिता की मौत के बाद संगमरमर से बना मकबरा भी तोड़ दिया गया था.

entertainment.title: Box Office: 'दृश्यम 3' को 'उड़ता तीर' ने गुरुवार को पछाड़ा, रजनीकांत की 'जेलर 2' साल की दूसरी धाकड़ फिल्म
entertainment.desc: रजनीकांत की फिल्म 'जेलर 2' ने 15 दिनों में ही रेकॉर्ड के नाम पर खूब झंडे गाड़े हैं। इस फिल्म ने जबरदस्त कमाई की और ये देश की दूसरी सबसे बड़ी फिल्म बन गई है। वहीं 'दृश्यम 3' ने भी साल की सबसे कमाऊ फिल्मों की लिस्ट में तीसरे नंबर पर जगह बनाई है। हालांकि, गुरुवार को आयुष्मान खुराना की 'उड़ता तीर' आगे निकल गई।

entertainment.title: Eetha Trailer: पैर में घुंघरू, नाक में नथ और नौवारी साड़ी... 'ईठा' में श्रद्धा कपूर का मैजिकल लुक
entertainment.desc: Shraddha Kapoor Eetha Trailer: श्रद्धा कपूर की मचअवेटेड फिल्म 'ईठा' का धमाकेदार ट्रेलर रिलीज हो गया है. जिसमें वो अपने डांस का हुनर दिखा रही हैं.

entertainment.title: 'जो सिस्टम के खिलाफ बोलता है उसे काम नहीं', भाई की मौत और NEET पेपर लीक पर राजेश कुमार ने सुनाई भतीजी की कहानी
entertainment.desc: टीवी एक्टर राजेश कुमार ने NEET पेपर लीक से जुड़े अपने परिवार के दर्दनाक अनुभव को साझा किया। उन्होंने बताया कि उनकी भतीजी को अपने पिता की मौत के महज 13 दिन बाद दोबारा NEET परीक्षा देनी पड़ी थी।

entertainment.title: बेटे युग संग अजमेर शरीफ की दरगाह में फंसे थे अजय देवगन, भीड़ पर फूटा गुस्सा, वायरल हो रहा Video

entertainment.title: परिणीति ने बादलों के पार 35,000 फीट ऊंचाई पर तोड़ा करवा चौथ का व्रत, कभी प्रियंका चोपड़ा ने भी यही किया था

general.title: Gold prices plunge to one-year low below $3,900 as higher oil prices fuel fears of more pain ahead
general.desc: (Kitco News) - The gold market has taken a big hit heading into the weekend, with prices breaking convincingly below $4,000 an ounce and falling to their lowest levels in more than a year.Gold's sharp selloff Friday pushed prices to their lowest level since October 6, 2025, when the precious metal touched an intraday low of $3,884.61 an ounce. The latest decline comes as investors brace for another potentially volatile week, with U.S. employment data and the midterm elections expected to provide fresh uncertainty for financial markets.According to analysts and traders, there is significant frustration in the marketplace as gold faces substantial selling pressure even as the U.S. dollar and bond yields weaken. (Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.) Traditionally, these two factors should be bullish for the precious metal, as they reduce its opportunity costs.Spot gold last traded at $3,880 an ounce, down 3.5% on the day; prices are down nearly 3% on the week. Silver is experiencing an even bigger drop, with prices falling below $50 an ounce. Spot silver last traded at $48.95 an ounce, down nearly 6% on the day. Silver prices are down nearly 9% since last Friday, marking their worst weekly decline since early June.Analysts have said that gold has been unable to find any bullish traction, even with lower bond yields, because of broader concerns in the marketplace.Although the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged following its monetary policy meeting Wednesday, the central bank remains committed to bringing inflation down. Looking beyond this week's pause, markets still expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December and through the first quarter of 2027.Philip Streible, Chief Market Strategist at Blue Line Futures, said that gold will continue to struggle as the ongoing war with Iran keeps oil prices elevated.“The rule in the markets is that you are supposed to buy the inflation and oil right now is the inflation,” he said.Streible added that gold performs well when the central bank is forced to cut interest rates to support the economy. However, with the economy expanding by 3.4% in the third quarter, he said the U.S. central bank has plenty of room to raise rates.“If the economy stays strong the Fed can continue to raise interest rates, which means gold will continue to have a target on its back,” he said.Simon-Peter Massabni, Head of Business Development at XS.com, said that despite the weakness in the U.S. dollar and lower bond yields, gold is reacting to inflation expectations and the future path of interest rates.“The decisive factor will be whether incoming economic data prompt markets to reassess the interest-rate outlook, shifting expectations toward a pause in tightening or a resumption of rate cuts. Until then, gold is likely to remain under selling pressure, despite supportive factors that continue to underpin its medium- to long-term outlook,” he said.“I see three developments that could change the outlook. First, a gradual but clear cooling in the US labor market, reflected in weaker job growth, rising unemployment, and slower wage growth. Second, a sustained decline in inflation, particularly core inflation and price components that capture the pass-through of higher energy costs into broader goods and services. Third, a downward repricing of future interest rate expectations and real yields.”Looking at gold's technical price action, Waleed Said, Technical Analyst at GivTrade, said that the path of least resistance remains lower. He added that he expects gold prices to eventually test support at $3,800 an ounce.The latest selloff has also pushed gold significantly below its 200-day moving average, which stands near $4,490 an ounce. With prices trading roughly 13.5% below this long-term trend indicator, the technical picture continues to reflect significant bearish momentum.“The mechanism matters here. It is not that people are swapping their gold for oil,” Said said. “Higher oil means higher inflation, higher inflation keeps central banks hawkish. On top of that, when the tech selloff hit, people sold gold to cover margin calls elsewhere. Gold is liquid, so it is the first thing that gets sold when people need cash. So in this war gold is not acting as the safe haven people expect. Oil and the dollar are taking that role.”With all the attention on inflation and oil prices, Naeem Aslam, CIO of Zaye Capital Markets, said that next week's midterm elections could have an impact on the outlook.Some political analysts have said that if Democrats regain control of Congress, winning majorities in both the House and Senate, it could become more difficult for the Trump administration to continue its war with Iran.Analysts have said that anything that eases tensions in the Middle East and ends the global energy supply crunch could be positive for gold.Aslam said he still expects any major dip in gold prices to represent a long-term buying opportunity.Jeff Sarti, CEO of Morton Wealth, said that he also sees a buying opportunity for gold, as the latest selloff appears to be a technical move.“DSI sentiment is flashing very bearish, which from a contrarian point of view indicates that this may be a strong entry point,” he said.Sarti added that he is also not concerned about gold's broken correlation with bond yields over the past week.“Much of the reason why yields are moderating is that there has been a sentiment shift away from the mega cap tech stocks into the safety net of bonds. But, the counter is that the latest GDP data was strong, implying that bond yields should be higher as opposed to lower. So, I think that there is some short-term noise, tied to stock market sentiment, pushing bond yields lower, as opposed to the assumption that the odds of interest rate hikes are moderating,” he said.Looking ahead, investors will have plenty of potential catalysts to navigate as financial markets remain volatile. Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections could have significant implications for the ongoing conflict with Iran and the outlook for energy prices, while Friday's nonfarm payrolls report will provide an important update on the health of the U.S. labor market.With gold struggling to attract safe-haven demand and inflation concerns keeping the Federal Reserve on a tightening path, analysts expect the precious metal to remain sensitive to shifting interest-rate expectations and broader market sentiment.Economic data to watch next week:Monday: ISM Manufacturing PMITuesday: US JOLTS job openings, mid-term electionsWednesday: ADP nonfarm payrolls, ISM Services PMIThursday: Bank of England monetary policy meeting, US weekly jobless claimsFriday: US nonfarm payrolls, University of Michigan preliminary Consumer Sentiment surveySee live precious metals prices for gold, silver, platinum and palladium — in USD, CAD and 12 more currencies.

business.title: Wall Street abandons ship after gold sinks below $3,900/oz, Main Street maintains bullish majority bias as midterms, payrolls loom
business.desc: (Kitco News) – Gold prices suffered another sharp weekly decline, as an early recovery gave way to heavy selling after the Federal Reserve maintained its hawkish stance, stronger U.S. economic data reinforced expectations for further tightening, and Friday's technology-led equity rout triggered widespread liquidation across precious metals.Spot gold kicked off the week trading at $3,994.95 per ounce on Sunday evening, and the yellow metal initially pushed higher as bargain-hunting emerged following the previous week's selloff below $4,000. The recovery gathered momentum Tuesday as Treasury yields eased and the U.S. dollar softened, carrying gold back above $4,050 ahead of Wednesday's Federal Reserve policy decision. After the Fed voted 10-2 to hold interest rates steady at 3.75% to 4.00%, with two policymakers dissenting in favor of another 25-basis-point hike, spot prices ultimately set their weekly high at $4,082.50 per ounce just before the equity close on Wednesday, before sellers regained control.Gold came under renewed pressure Thursday after stronger-than-expected third-quarter GDP growth and elevated core PCE inflation reinforced expectations that further monetary tightening could be necessary. The metal slipped back toward $4,000 as the dollar remained supported, despite some relief from easing Treasury yields and lower oil prices.Selling accelerated dramatically on Friday as a sharp decline in technology stocks, driven by growing concerns over returns on artificial intelligence investment, triggered broader market liquidations. Gold broke decisively below $4,000 and continued falling alongside silver and other precious metals, as forced selling and expectations for another Fed rate hike overwhelmed safe-haven demand. Spot gold ultimately set its weekly low of $3,870.25 per ounce late Friday afternoon – its weakest level in more than a year – and was trading only a few dollars above that level heading into the close.The latest Kitco News Weekly Gold Survey showed Wall Street bulls abandoning ship after gold sank below $3,900, while Main Street maintained a narrow bullish majority bias despite the yellow metal’s price rout.“Gold’s shine has dulled,” said Marc Chandler, managing director at Bannockburn Global Forex. “The yellow metal was near $4700 as recently as late August. The one caveat is that the once-more precious metal is below the lower Bollinger Band (two standard deviations below the 20-day moving average. Still, there does not appear to have been a capitulation trade, and assuming a push to new lows for the year, I suspect gold can fall into the $3750-$3850 range.”“Lower,” said Adam Button, head of currency strategy at investingLive. “It's a big week with the midterms and the potential resumption of the Iran war, but I fear that Trump could lash out and escalate, leading to a severe risk-off trade.”“I am bearish on Gold for the coming week,” said Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management. “Technically, the breakdown below $4,000 is significant.”“Unchanged,” said Rich Checkan, president and COO of Asset Strategies International. “I see competing influences this coming week. Renewed strikes on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz may bring retaliation soon after U.S. mid-term elections. That should push oil prices higher and stoke inflation concerns… putting downward pressure on gold. But if Democrats make gains in the mid-term elections, it may very well drive uneasy Republicans to the safety and protection of gold.”“I would treat every drop in gold prices as an opportunity to buy well,” Checkan added.Daniel Pavilonis, senior commodities broker at StoneX Group, told Kitco News that now that gold and silver have broken near-term critical support, the precious metals may be in for a longer and deeper correction, and gold will need some indication of easing monetary policy to resume the upward trajectory of the last couple of years.“We're still seeing some inflation,” he said. “We're seeing equities sell off. We're seeing commodities have come off, except for some of the energy sector.Pavilonis said the market is in the midst of an unwind. “If you're looking at the charts, they don't look so hot... If you're just looking at this from a technical standpoint, not any fundamentals, it looks like we could go lower.”As for how low the precious metals could slide, Pavilonis said the metals could be in for a deep pullback before sustained buying resumes.“I could see silver getting as low as the high $30s,” he said. “I could see gold getting as low as somewhere around $3,000. I think it's very likely to happen into the first quarter of next year, and then maybe just base out for a little while, and then possibly move higher.”Pavilonis said he’s seen this time and time again. “What happened the last few times when silver hit $50, when gold spikes up? We sell off afterward,” he said. “The party is over. The themes that we [saw at the early 2026 highs], the same headlines, the same stories… because of inflation, because of this or that. People need to rationalize why it went up so much. But if you go back into the archives and look at news around 1980 – before people realized it was the Hunt brothers, which was part of the story – but it was the same thing: ‘We're running out of silver, we're running out of gold, the exchanges are low, warehouses are low, inventories… And people are buying, and so you’ve got to go out and buy some gold, go out and buy some silver!’ There were almost identical New York Times articles being written about silver and gold in the run-up to 1980.”“Now I think that anybody from the move to the upside that hasn't been stopped out, or is holding on the physical side, It's time to hedge,” he said. “You want to start collaring around positions. You want to start collaring and capitalizing on it. Because if it does go lower, then there's ways to mitigate that, put yourself in the right position where you can accumulate more. That's what I would be thinking about right now.”Pavilonis said that if we see further liquidations across financial markets, he expects to see more selling of gold as well.“We have this rationale to buy and hold onto the metals,” he said. “I think in the long term you're going to be right. But in the short term, the thesis can be wrong, so it's time to maybe even hedge a little bit further if you haven't already.”This week, 16 analysts participated in the Kitco News Gold Survey, with Wall Street’s bullish belief all but evaporating after gold couldn’t hold $3,900. Only one expert, or 6%, expected to see gold prices gain ground during the week ahead, while 10, representing 63%, saw the yellow metal declining further. The remaining five analysts, 31% of the total, said they couldn’t predict gold’s direction, or expected sideways trading next week.Meanwhile, 184 votes were cast in Kitco’s online poll, with Main Street investors once again more bullish than their professional counterparts despite gold’s steep selloff. 98 retail traders, or 53%, looked for gold prices to rise next week, while 56 others, or 30%, predicted the yellow metal would lose further ground. The remaining 30 investors, representing 16% of the total, expected to see price consolidation during the week ahead.Next week will feature top-tier economic data and geopolitical risk events for investors to navigate, with the U.S. midterm elections and October’s nonfarm payrolls report the most significant of a raft of market-movers.The week begins with the Monday morning release of ISM Manufacturing PMI for October. Then on Tuesday markets will receive JOLTS job openings as ongoing mid-term election voting dominates the news.Wednesday will offer the second reading of U.S. employment with ADP’s private nonfarm payrolls, followed by the ISM Services PMI. Then on Thursday, traders will watch for the Bank of England’s monetary policy decision, along with weekly jobless claims data.The week wraps up Friday morning with the publication of October nonfarm payrolls, followed by the University of Michigan’s preliminary Consumer Sentiment survey.  Jesse Colombo, independent precious metals analyst and founder of the BubbleBubble Report, told Kitco News that gold and silver are testing key support zones which, if definitively breached, could result in a broad capitulation in precious metals.Colombo said Friday’s price action is somewhat unusual, because it's not driven by a clear surge in the dollar.“You also have Treasury yields falling, and bond yields overall falling,” he said. “Oil is up, so that could certainly be a factor, but it's not really up in such an extreme way, about 2% to 2.5%. It doesn't seem like the sell-off in gold is commensurate with the rise in oil.”“There's definitely a technical element,” he said. “I suspect there's risk aversion heading into the midterms, and also there's liquidations in tech stocks.”Colombo said there’s also trepidation that the U.S. administration may escalate the Iran conflict.“I've even seen some speculation that there could be some action this weekend,” he said. “A lot of times President Trump likes to kick things off on the weekend, have a quick skirmish, and then wrap it up by Sunday evening before the futures open. It's possible that there's risk aversion ahead of this weekend, like ‘sell first, ask questions later.’”Colombo warned that negative sentiment has resulted in a snowballing of downside momentum which could soon lead to a capitulation.“It's taking out these key support levels,” he said. “For example, on COMEX gold futures, $3,900 to $4,000 was that floor of support that I've been watching, and that was formed exactly one year ago, in October and November, that support zone. It's testing that zone, but it has not broken below it yet.”Colombo said he’ll also be watching Friday’s close and how the new week begins.“Does it continue to hold this zone? We're really at a critical level,” he said. “If it does indeed close below on strong volume – possibly next week – then the next support I'm looking at is around $3,500.”“I'm not saying it will go there. I'm just saying if this current support indeed fails, the next level to watch is $3,500.”For silver, Colombo is keeping his eye on the 45-55 support zone in COMEX futures, which was also formed during the October-November highs and lows exactly one year ago.“That was the last area where it was consolidating and bouncing around before that big parabolic run-up into late 2025, early 2026, so I want to see how it acts there,” he said. “Plus $50, which has played such a key role going back to 1980, roughly the peak of the 1970s secular bull market in silver and precious metals, and then 2011 as well.”“In November 2025, silver shot above that, and I viewed that as a sign of a major multi-year breakout,” Colombo said. “Now we're approaching $50 from the upside, and now it's a new support – not literally $50, but a zone around there, because you know there’s going to be all sorts of shenanigans at that level. I want to see if it's going to hold; It can go a little bit below there, a quick flush. If it holds it, good. If it breaks below, we look to the next support. But for now, it's still holding that support, so that’s what I'm banking on at the moment.”Alex Kuptsikevich, senior market analyst at FxPro, expects gold prices to fall further next week.“Gold has now been in a downtrend for almost two and a half months, continuing to form an almost perfect line of resistance through a series of progressively lower local highs,” he noted. “On Friday, the spot price of a troy ounce plummeted to $3,940, rewriting the lows seen since last November and breaking through the support zone (just below $4,000) that had halted the sell-off in June and July. Of the entire recent uptrend, starting from the lows four years ago to the highs in January and February, the price has now corrected by 61.8% of that rise, meaning it has reached the lower boundary of a classic correction.”“However, we view the immediate short-term outlook with some concern,” Kuptsikevich warned. “The decline in gold is accompanied by substantial sell-offs in the stock markets; in other words, this is a typical flight from risk amid potential margin calls, with few paying attention to prices and merely rebalancing their positions to normal levels. Although gold is generally regarded as a safe-haven asset, it tends to move in tandem with equity markets during such sell-offs and only turns upwards after signals from central banks that monetary policy is shifting towards easing.”Kuptsikevich said that while the Fed, the ECB and the Bank of Japan did not raise interest rates this week, they reinforced expectations of a December hike. “At the same time, oil, a leading indicator of inflation in the current economic climate, is approaching the upper limit of this year’s trading range, promising increased pressure on prices,” he noted. “It is clear that the inverse correlation between oil and gold seen four years ago has returned: the higher oil prices, the lower the gold prices. And we find ourselves having to dust off our original scenario for gold, which we have maintained since the start of the year, which predicted a fall in the price of a troy ounce to $3,300.”Neil Welsh, head of metals at Britannia Global Markets, said gold prices have declined against the backdrop of technology-sector losses, higher energy prices and changing interest rate expectations. “These are overlapping influences rather than evidence of a single driver,” he said. “Gold’s safe-haven reputation does not make it immune to the market’s demand for cash.”“The clearest catalyst for a change would be a material deterioration in US economic activity, particularly in the labour market, that leads markets to price out further rate hikes and pushes real yields lower,” Welsh said. “A central-bank pause alone is unlikely to be enough. Both the Fed and the ECB have maintained a conditional bias towards further tightening, so gold needs evidence of a genuine shift in the policy outlook, rather than simply a wait for more data.”Welsh said next Friday’s nonfarm payrolls report will be an important test for markets. “A weak reading, particularly if accompanied by slower wage growth, higher unemployment or downward revisions to previous figures, could substantially reduce expectations of a December rate hike and create a more supportive macroeconomic backdrop for gold,” he said. “However, a single release may not be enough if inflation stays elevated and the broader economy remains resilient. In that case, any recovery could prove to be a tactical rebound within an ongoing period of consolidation.”At the time of writing, spot gold last traded at $3,875.05 per ounce for a loss of 3.74% on the week and 3.62% on the day.See live precious metals prices for gold, silver, platinum and palladium — in USD, CAD and 12 more currencies.

business.title: Gold falls below $3,900, silver tumbles as Wall Street selloff triggers liquidation - Kitco PM Report
business.desc: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Friday, as a technology-led equity market selloff intensified liquidation pressure across precious metals, offsetting the support normally provided by falling Treasury yields and heightened geopolitical uncertainty. Crude oil prices climbed more than 2% following another tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to inflation concerns and expectations that Federal Reserve monetary policy will remain restrictive. Spot gold was trading near $3,879.90 an ounce, down $141.60, or 3.52%, while spot silver was trading near $49.015, down $3.150, or 6.06%, on the session.Friday's U.S. economic reports presented a mixed picture of moderating wage growth and weakening regional manufacturing activity. The employment cost index increased 0.8% in the third quarter, matching expectations and slowing from 0.9% in the second quarter. The October Chicago purchasing managers' index declined to 55.3 from 58.8 in September, missing expectations near 56.1 but remaining above the 50-point threshold separating expansion from contraction. Friday's softer wage and manufacturing readings followed Thursday's stronger-than-expected third-quarter gross domestic product report, which showed the U.S. economy expanding at a 3.4% annualized pace, compared with 2.2% in the second quarter. September headline personal consumption expenditures inflation accelerated to 3.6% annually, while core PCE inflation increased to 3.1%, reinforcing concerns about persistent underlying price pressure.Market positioning remains divided between resilient economic growth, persistent inflation and the growing risk of financial-market instability. The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00% Wednesday, with two policymakers favoring an immediate 25-basis-point increase. Interest rate futures continued to reflect substantial expectations for further tightening in December, although Friday's moderating employment costs and sharp equity-market decline provided counterweights to the inflationary implications of strong GDP growth and higher energy prices. Treasury yields fell as investors sought the relative safety of government bonds, with the benchmark 10-year yield retreating toward 4.93% and the two-year yield approaching 4.58%. However, gold continued to decline, suggesting that forced liquidation, portfolio rebalancing and the broader outlook for restrictive monetary policy outweighed immediate safe-haven demand.The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation remained a major source of energy-market uncertainty Friday after another commercial tanker was attacked in the strategic waterway. The vessel was struck by explosive devices attached to its hull by a small boat, highlighting the continuing vulnerability of commercial shipping despite regional diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions. Responsibility for the attack had not been established. The incident intensified concerns that renewed military confrontation involving Iran and the United States could further disrupt Middle Eastern energy exports, particularly as markets assessed the possibility of additional military action following the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Negotiations involving Washington, Tehran and regional mediators have yet to produce a confirmed settlement, leaving disagreements over sanctions, maritime security and the future of commercial access through Hormuz unresolved.Crude oil futures rose more than 2% Friday, reaching their highest settlements since late April as traders assessed the possibility of renewed disruptions to Gulf energy supplies. December Brent crude futures gained $2.76, or 2.4%, to settle at $117.64 a barrel after reaching $118.00 intraday. The more actively traded January Brent contract advanced $2.63 to $113.43, while Nymex WTI futures increased $2.12, or 2.08%, to settle at $104.12. Brent gained approximately 13.6% during October, while WTI rose 15.2%, reflecting persistent concerns about Middle Eastern supply security and the inflationary consequences of the regional conflict.For gold, the latest Hormuz attack reinforced underlying geopolitical demand, but higher crude prices also heightened the risk that inflation will remain persistent and the Federal Reserve will maintain restrictive monetary policy. The sharp decline in bullion despite falling Treasury yields indicates that broader financial-market liquidation was the more immediate influence on Friday's trading. Silver suffered considerably greater losses as weakness in precious metals coincided with concerns about industrial demand, equity-market valuations and restrictive financing conditions. The widening gold-silver ratio reflected silver's greater sensitivity to deteriorating risk sentiment and concerns about manufacturing activity.North American equity markets finished sharply lower Friday as disappointing corporate earnings and concerns about artificial intelligence-related investment triggered heavy selling in technology shares. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined approximately 1.1% to close at 51,770.31, while the S&P 500 fell 1.8% to 7,580.07, its largest daily decline since June. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.9% to finish near 25,437, as weakness in semiconductor and major technology shares dominated trading. Intel plunged nearly 29% following disappointing profit guidance, while concerns surrounding Amazon's capital spending added to pressure on the technology sector. The Russell 2000 declined 1.7% to 2,811.84, indicating that selling extended beyond large-cap growth companies. Canada's S&P/TSX Composite Index also fell sharply, losing more than 2% as weakness in precious metals mining and other resource shares compounded the broader deterioration in risk sentiment.European equity markets closed mostly lower Friday as technology-sector weakness and concerns about elevated energy prices weighed on investor sentiment. The pan-European Stoxx 600 declined approximately 0.4% to 646.73, while Germany's DAX lost 0.9% to finish near 25,819. France's CAC 40 slipped 0.1% to approximately 7,962, while the U.K.'s FTSE 100 outperformed, advancing 0.1% to around 10,736. The Euro Stoxx 50 fell approximately 1.2%, reflecting heavier losses among major continental companies. European technology shares were particularly weak as the U.S. semiconductor selloff affected global valuations, while higher crude prices added to concerns about inflation, corporate margins and the outlook for regional monetary policy. Despite Friday's losses, the Stoxx 600 finished October higher, reflecting gains earlier in the month.The key outside markets see Nymex WTI crude oil futures higher and settling at $104.12 a barrel, while December Brent crude futures finished at $117.64. business.title: Gold prices plunge to one-year low below $3,900 as higher oil prices fuel fears of more pain ahead
business.desc: (Kitco News) - The gold market has taken a big hit heading into the weekend, with prices breaking convincingly below $4,000 an ounce and falling to their lowest levels in more than a year.Gold's sharp selloff Friday pushed prices to their lowest level since October 6, 2025, when the precious metal touched an intraday low of $3,884.61 an ounce. The latest decline comes as investors brace for another potentially volatile week, with U.S. employment data and the midterm elections expected to provide fresh uncertainty for financial markets.According to analysts and traders, there is significant frustration in the marketplace as gold faces substantial selling pressure even as the U.S. dollar and bond yields weaken. (Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.) Traditionally, these two factors should be bullish for the precious metal, as they reduce its opportunity costs.Spot gold last traded at $3,880 an ounce, down 3.5% on the day; prices are down nearly 3% on the week. Silver is experiencing an even bigger drop, with prices falling below $50 an ounce. Spot silver last traded at $48.95 an ounce, down nearly 6% on the day. Silver prices are down nearly 9% since last Friday, marking their worst weekly decline since early June.Analysts have said that gold has been unable to find any bullish traction, even with lower bond yields, because of broader concerns in the marketplace.Although the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged following its monetary policy meeting Wednesday, the central bank remains committed to bringing inflation down. Looking beyond this week's pause, markets still expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December and through the first quarter of 2027.Philip Streible, Chief Market Strategist at Blue Line Futures, said that gold will continue to struggle as the ongoing war with Iran keeps oil prices elevated.“The rule in the markets is that you are supposed to buy the inflation and oil right now is the inflation,” he said.Streible added that gold performs well when the central bank is forced to cut interest rates to support the economy. However, with the economy expanding by 3.4% in the third quarter, he said the U.S. central bank has plenty of room to raise rates.“If the economy stays strong the Fed can continue to raise interest rates, which means gold will continue to have a target on its back,” he said.Simon-Peter Massabni, Head of Business Development at XS.com, said that despite the weakness in the U.S. dollar and lower bond yields, gold is reacting to inflation expectations and the future path of interest rates.“The decisive factor will be whether incoming economic data prompt markets to reassess the interest-rate outlook, shifting expectations toward a pause in tightening or a resumption of rate cuts. Until then, gold is likely to remain under selling pressure, despite supportive factors that continue to underpin its medium- to long-term outlook,” he said.“I see three developments that could change the outlook. First, a gradual but clear cooling in the US labor market, reflected in weaker job growth, rising unemployment, and slower wage growth. Second, a sustained decline in inflation, particularly core inflation and price components that capture the pass-through of higher energy costs into broader goods and services. Third, a downward repricing of future interest rate expectations and real yields.”Looking at gold's technical price action, Waleed Said, Technical Analyst at GivTrade, said that the path of least resistance remains lower. He added that he expects gold prices to eventually test support at $3,800 an ounce.The latest selloff has also pushed gold significantly below its 200-day moving average, which stands near $4,490 an ounce. With prices trading roughly 13.5% below this long-term trend indicator, the technical picture continues to reflect significant bearish momentum.“The mechanism matters here. It is not that people are swapping their gold for oil,” Said said. “Higher oil means higher inflation, higher inflation keeps central banks hawkish. On top of that, when the tech selloff hit, people sold gold to cover margin calls elsewhere. Gold is liquid, so it is the first thing that gets sold when people need cash. So in this war gold is not acting as the safe haven people expect. Oil and the dollar are taking that role.”With all the attention on inflation and oil prices, Naeem Aslam, CIO of Zaye Capital Markets, said that next week's midterm elections could have an impact on the outlook.Some political analysts have said that if Democrats regain control of Congress, winning majorities in both the House and Senate, it could become more difficult for the Trump administration to continue its war with Iran.Analysts have said that anything that eases tensions in the Middle East and ends the global energy supply crunch could be positive for gold.Aslam said he still expects any major dip in gold prices to represent a long-term buying opportunity.Jeff Sarti, CEO of Morton Wealth, said that he also sees a buying opportunity for gold, as the latest selloff appears to be a technical move.“DSI sentiment is flashing very bearish, which from a contrarian point of view indicates that this may be a strong entry point,” he said.Sarti added that he is also not concerned about gold's broken correlation with bond yields over the past week.“Much of the reason why yields are moderating is that there has been a sentiment shift away from the mega cap tech stocks into the safety net of bonds. But, the counter is that the latest GDP data was strong, implying that bond yields should be higher as opposed to lower. So, I think that there is some short-term noise, tied to stock market sentiment, pushing bond yields lower, as opposed to the assumption that the odds of interest rate hikes are moderating,” he said.Looking ahead, investors will have plenty of potential catalysts to navigate as financial markets remain volatile. Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections could have significant implications for the ongoing conflict with Iran and the outlook for energy prices, while Friday's nonfarm payrolls report will provide an important update on the health of the U.S. labor market.With gold struggling to attract safe-haven demand and inflation concerns keeping the Federal Reserve on a tightening path, analysts expect the precious metal to remain sensitive to shifting interest-rate expectations and broader market sentiment.Economic data to watch next week:Monday: ISM Manufacturing PMITuesday: US JOLTS job openings, mid-term electionsWednesday: ADP nonfarm payrolls, ISM Services PMIThursday: Bank of England monetary policy meeting, US weekly jobless claimsFriday: US nonfarm payrolls, University of Michigan preliminary Consumer Sentiment surveySee live precious metals prices for gold, silver, platinum and palladium — in USD, CAD and 12 more currencies.

business.title: Gold drops below $4,000, silver tumbles as Hormuz attack lifts oil prices - Kitco AM Report
business.desc: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Friday, as renewed attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed crude oil prices higher and reinforced inflation concerns despite fresh evidence of moderating U.S. wage growth. Precious metals remained under selling pressure following Thursday's declines, with gold slipping below $4,000.00 an ounce and silver falling to its lowest levels of the year. Spot gold was trading near $3,958.80 an ounce, down $61.34, or 1.32%, while spot silver was trading near $50.080, down $2.120, or 4,06%. Gold was heading toward a second consecutive monthly decline, while silver continued to underperform amid concerns about industrial demand and restrictive monetary policy.The latest U.S. employment cost figures provided some evidence that labor-related inflation pressure is moderating, although wage growth remains elevated. The employment cost index increased 0.8% in the third quarter, matching expectations and slowing from 0.9% in the second quarter. Wages and salaries increased 0.7%, compared with 0.9% in the previous quarter, while benefit costs rose 0.9%, down from 1.0%. Total compensation costs increased 3.4% from a year earlier, unchanged from the annual rate recorded in June, while wages and salaries rose 3.1% and benefit costs increased 3.9%. The slowdown in quarterly wage growth provides some relief from concerns about persistent labor-cost inflation, although annual compensation growth remains above levels consistent with the Federal Reserve's longer-term inflation objective.The employment report followed Thursday's stronger-than-expected third-quarter gross domestic product figures and another increase in the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge. The U.S. economy expanded at a 3.4% annualized pace in the third quarter, accelerating from 2.2% in the second quarter, supported by resilient consumer spending and business investment. September headline personal consumption expenditures inflation increased 0.5% on the month and 3.6% annually, while core PCE inflation rose 0.3% and 3.1%, respectively. The combination of accelerating economic growth and persistent underlying inflation continues to complicate the case for easier monetary policy, even as Friday's wage figures suggest some moderation in labor costs.Market positioning remains focused on the possibility of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December following Wednesday's decision to leave the benchmark federal funds target range unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00%. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to maintain rates, with two policymakers favoring an immediate 25-basis-point increase. Futures markets assigned approximately an 83% probability to a December increase following Thursday's GDP and inflation releases, with the latest wage data providing some counterweight to those expectations. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield declined 7 basis points Thursday to approximately 4.98%, as weakness in major technology shares encouraged demand for government bonds. However, gold continued to fall despite lower yields, reflecting the influence of persistent inflation concerns, expectations for further tightening and broader precious metals liquidation.The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation deteriorated further Friday following another attack on a commercial tanker in the strategic waterway, highlighting the continuing risks to Middle Eastern energy supplies. Maritime security authorities confirmed that a tanker was struck by explosive devices attached to its hull by a small boat, although responsibility for the incident had not been established. The attack came amid persistent threats to regional shipping and uncertainty about the prospects for renewed negotiations between Washington and Tehran. Diplomatic initiatives involving Qatar and other regional mediators have yet to produce an agreement, while disagreements over sanctions, maritime security and the broader conflict continue to prevent a lasting settlement.Crude oil prices rose sharply following the latest attack, with December Brent futures climbing toward $117.15 a barrel and WTI advancing to approximately $103.79. Brent was heading toward a monthly gain of approximately 13%, while WTI was on course for an increase of around 15%, reflecting sustained concerns about Gulf energy supplies and the possibility of further military escalation. The risk of renewed confrontation has become particularly important ahead of the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, with uncertainty surrounding the next phase of U.S.-Iran relations adding to the geopolitical premium embedded in crude prices. Although alternative export routes have helped mitigate some of the disruption to Gulf petroleum shipments, continued tanker attacks and elevated maritime security costs remain significant obstacles to restoring normal commercial flows through Hormuz.For gold, the continuing confrontation supports defensive demand, but the inflationary consequences of elevated crude oil prices have reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may need to maintain restrictive monetary policy for longer. The metal's continued decline despite geopolitical instability and lower Treasury yields suggests that liquidation pressure and the interest rate outlook remain dominant influences on near-term price action. Silver has suffered significantly greater losses as the broader precious metals decline coincides with concerns about industrial demand, elevated energy costs and restrictive borrowing conditions. Its break below previously established technical support has added to selling pressure, leaving the metal increasingly vulnerable to further liquidation.Global equity markets were weaker before the U.S. open as disappointing corporate earnings and renewed concerns about artificial intelligence investment weighed on technology shares. S&P 500 futures declined approximately 1.0%, while Nasdaq futures dropped 2.3% and Dow futures were little changed. Alphabet's sharp decline Thursday was followed by additional pressure on major technology companies after cautious earnings guidance from Amazon and Intel. European equity markets were mixed, while Asian markets were mostly lower as investors assessed corporate earnings, higher energy prices and the outlook for global monetary policy. The combination of rising crude prices, elevated financing costs and uncertainty surrounding large-scale artificial intelligence investment continued to undermine risk appetite, although the resulting demand for government bonds provided limited support for precious metals.The key outside markets see Nymex WTI crude oil prices higher and trading near $103.79 a barrel, while December Brent crude futures were near $117.15, reflecting renewed concerns about Gulf energy supplies. The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note was trading near the 5.0% area following Thursday's decline.
